I will think about this year the way I always do — starting from what I did last year, because last year my wheat gave me a bit over 450 jin per mu (about 450 kg/mu) and the maize was around 1100 jin (550 kg/mu). Not bad. No reason to change much.

My land is 10.7 mu, all wheat-maize rotation like everyone in our village. I have my own well, so water is not my worry — fertilizer and seed cost is what I count.

**Wheat (winter crop, October to June):**
I buy the improved seed from the same dealer in town — the one most neighbors use. I don't plant the old varieties anymore, nobody does. I use about 15 kg seed per mu, maybe a little more because I sow late sometimes.

For base fertilizer before sowing, I put down 2 bags of compound 15-15-15 per mu — that's 100 kg. Then in spring when the wheat greens up, I spread urea, about 20 kg per mu (half a bag), together with the spring irrigation. Some neighbors put more, some less. I don't want to lose yield so I put a bit extra rather than too little. Fertilizer costs money but a bad harvest costs more.

Water: once before winter (dong shui), once at green-up, once at jointing, sometimes one more at grain filling if it's dry. Usually 3 times, 4 if the sky doesn't give rain.

Pesticide: one spray for weeds in spring, one or two for aphids and the white powder disease (powdery mildew) near heading. Call it 3 sprays.

Tillage: after maize I use the rotary tiller — the village machine service does it, 40-50 yuan per mu. Faster than plowing and everyone does it.

**Maize (summer crop, June to September/October):**
Hybrid seed, I buy it fresh every year — Zhengdan or similar, whatever the dealer recommends that year. About 2-2.5 kg per mu.

I plant right after wheat harvest, no tillage, just direct seed into the stubble with the seeder. Saves time, saves money.

Base fertilizer with seeding: 1.5 bags compound per mu (75 kg). Then at the big-bell stage (da la kou) I topdress with urea, about 25 kg per mu. Maize eats more nitrogen, I learned this from watching — if you skimp, the leaves go yellow and the cob is small.

Water: maize gets summer rain but I still need to irrigate 2 times usually — once after sowing if dry, once at tasseling. Sometimes 3 if the summer is dry.

Pesticide: one for the borer worm, sometimes one more for armyworm if it comes. 2 sprays usually.

My whole year's fertilizer bill is the biggest worry — around 300 yuan per mu just for fertilizer, times 10.7 mu is over 3000 yuan. But I have 5 mouths to feed, I can't take chances with a small harvest.
